title: Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) for Spaceflight Life Support
measuredFact: Standard NASA planning reference rates: Oxygen consumption is 0.84 kg/person/day; nutritional dry food solids requirement is 0.62 kg/person/day; direct drinking water requirement is 1.62 kg/person/day (total hydration + food prep + hygiene is ~2.5–3.5 L/person/day).
gameAssumption: Outpost baseline for 4 crew: 3.2 kg O₂/day (0.80 kg/person), 12 L total potable water/day (3.0 L/person), and 6 kg wet food rations/day (1.5 kg/person).
simplificationRationale: Rounds numbers to clean decimals for junior astronaut cognitive accessibility while preserving exact physiological proportions and closed-loop demand ratios.

title: Oxygen Generation System (OGS) Flight Performance & Water Electrolysis Stoichiometry
authorOrMission: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center & ISS ECLSS Office
measuredFact: Water electrolysis converts deionized water into oxygen and hydrogen via 2 H2O -> 2 H2 + O2. Mass stoichiometry requires 1.125 kg of water per 1.0 kg of O2 produced (36 g H2O / 32 g O2). Operating cell power demand is ~4.0–6.0 kWh per kg O2.
gameAssumption: Generating 3.2 kg of O2 requires exactly 3.6 L of water and 19.2 kWh of electrical energy (6.0 kWh/kg).
simplificationRationale: Preserves exact chemical mass conservation: without water and electricity, oxygen generation is chemically impossible.

title: Exploration Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) Water Recovery
authorOrMission: NASA ISS Program (Exploration ECLSS WPA & Brine Processor Assembly)
measuredFact: NASA exploration ECLSS architecture establishes an initial baseline target of approximately 90% water recovery. In 2023, the ISS achieved a historic 98% water recovery milestone using the catalytic Water Processor Assembly combined with the Brine Processor Assembly (BPA).
gameAssumption: Artemis Base Alpha begins with an 80% water recovery efficiency, upgradeable to 90% (Level 2) and up to 99% (Level 3).
simplificationRationale: Allows commanders to experience the critical operational gap between low recycling (fast water depletion) and closed-loop mastery.

title: Orion Artemis I Cislunar Radiation Environment Flight Measurements
authorOrMission: NASA Human Research Program / HERA & MARE Experiments
measuredFact: Active sensors inside the uncrewed Orion spacecraft during the Artemis I mission measured a Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) dose-equivalent rate of 0.96–1.24 mSv/day in cislunar and lunar orbit. Solar Particle Events (SPEs) produce sudden proton flux increases delivering 15 to >100 mSv.
gameAssumption: Nominal background dose is set to 1.00 mSv/day (matching the Artemis I range). Solar storms add +15 to +35 mSv. Base aluminum hull offers 30% shielding, and sintered regolith shelters increase shielding to 50–90%.
simplificationRationale: Directly integrates Artemis I empirical flight data while modeling regolith mass attenuation without complex particle transport Monte Carlo code.

title: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Diviner Radiometer Surface Illumination Data
authorOrMission: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / UCLA
measuredFact: The Moon has a synodic day of ~29.53 Earth days. In non-polar terrain, a surface outpost experiences approximately 14 continuous Earth days (354 hours) of solar daylight followed by 14 continuous Earth days of total darkness, with surface temperatures dropping below -130°C.
gameAssumption: A 30-day lunar mission features Daylight on Days 1–14, Lunar Night on Days 15–28, and Dawn on Days 29–30.
simplificationRationale: Forces commanders to solve the premier lunar surface engineering challenge: storing enough battery reserve and managing power loads to survive two weeks of darkness.

title: LCROSS Impact Confirmation of Lunar South Pole Volatiles and Water Ice
authorOrMission: NASA Ames Research Center / Science Magazine (Colaprete et al., 2010)
measuredFact: The Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) impacted the permanently shadowed region (PSR) of Cabeus crater, detecting water vapor and ice crystals estimating approximately 5.5% ± 1.5% (approx. 6%) water ice by mass in the ejecta plume.
gameAssumption: Artemis Base Alpha is sited at the South Pole rim (Shackleton/Cabeus region), establishing the scientific premise for long-term water extraction and closed-loop hydrology.
simplificationRationale: Grounds the outpost's location and life support dependencies in confirmed lunar volatile discoveries.

title: NASA Veggie and Advanced Plant Habitat (APH) Space Crop Production Investigations
authorOrMission: NASA Kennedy Space Center / ISS Space Biology
measuredFact: The ISS Veggie production system accommodates approximately 6 plant pillows for fresh dietary supplements. The Advanced Plant Habitat (APH) is an automated, enclosed growth chamber supporting long-duration experiments lasting up to 135 days (e.g., dwarf wheat, chile peppers).
gameAssumption: Hydroponic greenhouse modules produce +4.0 kg fresh biomass food/day, consuming 6 kWh electrical lighting power and 16 L water/day.
simplificationRationale: Simulates agricultural balance where crops provide ongoing caloric production but introduce non-trivial water and electrical loads.

title: Human Exploration of Mars Design Reference Architecture 5.0
measuredFact: Mars orbits at ~1.52 AU from the Sun, reducing solar irradiance to ~590 W/m² (approximately 43% of Earth/Moon's 1361 W/m²). Atmospheric dust storms significantly increase optical depth (tau), reducing surface solar power by up to 80%.
gameAssumption: Mars campaign solar generation yields 32 kWh/sol (compared to 45 kWh/day on the Moon), with higher baseline heating demand and dust storm mitigation requirements.
simplificationRationale: Highlights the distinct planetary physics and engineering trade-offs when transitioning from lunar to Martian surface operations.
